claims.claim: Established characters keep their canonical pronouns regardless of species or type (Baphomet and Strahd he/him; Lolth and Tasha she/her).
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.claim: The 2021 docx adds creature types (Humanoid, Fey, Undead) to the capitalized game terms, a convention the 2019 PDF lacks.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.claim: Bold stat-block names are explained functionally: bold signals that the term is a game object to be looked up, so 'Strahd likes to make vampire spawn' stays roman.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: this indicates the term is a game object

claims.claim: Effects triggered by hitting must say 'attack roll', because readers read 'attack' in its English sense and think fireball 'hits'.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: The word “attack” confuses many of our readers

claims.claim: 'Within X feet' literally reaches through total cover, so writers must add a sight/hearing/cover condition or use an official area of effect.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: use one of our official areas of effect

claims.claim: The box of game information is called a stat block; 'statistics' is reserved for the crunch in the abstract.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.claim: Lists, spells, and bestiary stat blocks are ordered letter-by-letter, ignoring spaces, with a warning that Word sorts word-by-word.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.claim: The 2021 word list adds aasimar, blood red (contra Merriam-Webster), cyclopes, gold vs golden, insectile not insectoid, parlay vs parley, tabaxi, tenant vs tenet.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.feature: lowercase 'hit points' persists in the 2021 docx
claims.claim: The 2021 docx still writes 'hit points' lowercase in its examples, whereas the 2024 rules glossary capitalizes 'Hit Points', so even the internal 2021 guide predates 2024 house style.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: Anyone who touches the orb regains 3 hit points.

claims.claim: The AL adventure format prescribes boxed text only for a particularly important event, never for rooms or normalcy.
claims.source: DC Adventure Format v1.3.docx (Claire Hoffman / Ma'at Crook, 2023-11) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: Boxed text should be used very sparingly

claims.claim: Boxed text is capped at one or two brief descriptive sentences.
claims.source: DC Adventure Format v1.3.docx (Claire Hoffman / Ma'at Crook, 2023-11) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: no more than one or two brief and descriptive sentences

claims.claim: Boxed text narrates exciting events only; the substance of an encounter lives under the headings beneath it.
claims.source: DC Adventure Format v1.3.docx (Claire Hoffman / Ma'at Crook, 2023-11) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: only provide a narrative for exciting events

claims.claim: The template's own sample boxed text is two descriptive sentences plus a one-line spoken tag ('Go away!'), with sensory and comic detail carried by concrete nouns.
claims.source: DC Adventure Format v1.3.docx (Claire Hoffman / Ma'at Crook, 2023-11) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.feature: background keywords in caps and bold
claims.claim: In the Background section, keywords are capitalized and bolded at first appearance to flag the adventure's important elements for the DM.
claims.source: DC Adventure Format v1.3.docx (Claire Hoffman / Ma'at Crook, 2023-11) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: Keywords should be CAPITALIZED and BOLDED the FIRST time

claims.claim: Background must not bloat with backstory that is not ultimately important; the line between too little and too much exposition is explicit.
claims.source: DC Adventure Format v1.3.docx (Claire Hoffman / Ma'at Crook, 2023-11) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: doesn’t bloat the background with backstory that isn’t ultimately important

verdicts.trueWording: He/Him: Baphomet, Strahd; She/Her: Lolth, Tasha
verdicts.note: Raw docx (DnD House Style Guide.docx, sha256 5bbfff1c…) extracted from the pack ZIP. Under 'Pronouns for Specific Individuals': 'For a character in canon (famous hero, demon lord, powerful celestial, etc.), use the established pronouns for their identity, regardless of their species or type.' followed verbatim by 'He/Him: Baphomet, Strahd' and 'She/Her: Lolth, Tasha'. Every limb supported.

Quote is verbatim in the 'Terms to Capitalize' inventory of the 2021 docx (docProps/core.xml: created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, lastModifiedBy 'Bauer, Judy', modified 2021-07-06 — source attribution confirmed). But the docx makes no comparison to any 2019 PDF, and the ZIP contains no 2019 style-guide PDF (only DnD Standards.pdf, PDF title 'D&D Standards', CreationDate D:20200716). The 'adds … a convention the 2019 PDF lacks' limb is unverifiable from this URL.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that this is an addition the 2019 PDF lacks

verdicts.trueWording: Bold stat block names … this indicates the term is a game object
verdicts.note: Verbatim: 'Bold stat block names in running text to indicate what stat block to use for an encounter—this indicates the term is a game object.' The facing examples list 'Roman' cases including 'Strahd likes to make vampire spawn in his free time.' Both limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: The word “attack” confuses many of our readers
verdicts.note: Section 'Attack vs. Attack Roll': 'When an effect is triggered by an attack roll hitting or missing, use the term “attack roll” in the effect’s text, not just “attack.” The word “attack” confuses many of our readers, who often read it with its English meaning instead of as a rules term.' Fireball limb also explicit: 'there are readers who think fireball hits targets'.

verdicts.trueWording: use one of our official areas of effect: cone, cube, cylinder, line, or sphere
verdicts.note: Section '“Within X Feet”': 'that literally means the effect reaches anything within that area, even if there’s total cover in the way. If you want to limit the reach of such an effect, require that the target be able to see or hear the effect’s source or that the target can’t be behind total cover. Alternatively, use one of our official areas of effect…'. All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: When referring to a monster’s stat block, call it a stat block
verdicts.note: Section '“Statistics” vs. “Stat Block”': 'Don’t call it the creature’s statistics. Writing “game statistics” is acceptable if you’re referring to the monster’s crunch, rather than its story material, but use “stat block” when you mean that box of game information about the monster.' Both limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: We use letter-by-letter alphabetization. When comparing, ignore spaces
verdicts.note: Section 'Alphabetical Organization': 'lists, spells, stat blocks in a bestiary, etc. should all be organized alphabetically. We use letter-by-letter alphabetization. When comparing, ignore spaces…' plus 'Microsoft Word Warning. Microsoft Word’s handy alphabetization tool (Table < Sort) sorts paragraphs word-by-word, NOT letter-by-letter!' All three limbs supported.

All eight items are verbatim in the docx word list: 'aasimar (singular and plural)', 'blood red (contra Merriam-Websters; we’re matching CMOS 7.89)', 'cyclopes (plural of cyclops)', 'gold (made of gold)' / 'golden (the color of gold)', 'insectile (not insectoid)', 'parlay (exploit or transform)' / 'parley (confer or negotiate)', 'tabaxi (singular and plural)', 'tenant' / 'tenet'. The 'adds' limb — that the 2019 PDF lacked them — is nowhere in this document and no 2019 style-guide PDF is in the pack.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that these entries are 2021 additions relative to the 2019 PDF

verdicts.trueWording: Anyone who touches the orb regains 3 hit points.
verdicts.note: Quote is verbatim under 'Numerals in Rules Text', lowercase 'hit points'; the abbreviations table likewise reads 'hp / hit points' lowercase, so the first limb is well supported. The comparison to the 2024 rules glossary — and therefore the conclusion that the 2021 guide 'predates 2024 house style' — is not on this page; the document is silent on 2024.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that the 2024 rules glossary capitalizes “Hit Points”

verdicts.trueWording: Boxed text should be used very sparingly—only when a particularly important event truly calls for it
verdicts.note: Raw docx (DC Adventure Format v1.3.docx, sha256 73965593…; core.xml: creator Claire Hoffman, lastModifiedBy Ma'at Crook, created 2023-11-07, modified 2023-11-16 — attribution confirmed). Boxed-text instruction continues 'Don’t use it to describe rooms or normalcy.' The document is the D&D Adventurers League (Dungeoncraft, code '$$-DC-$$$-$$') adventure template, so the 'AL adventure format' framing holds.

verdicts.trueWording: no more than one or two brief and descriptive sentences
verdicts.note: Same boxed-text instruction: 'Additionally, it should be short and to the point, no more than one or two brief and descriptive sentences.'

verdicts.trueWording: the boxed text should only provide a narrative for exciting events
verdicts.note: 'The body of the counter [sic — encounter] should be found in the headings below; the boxed text should only provide a narrative for exciting events.' Both limbs supported; note the source's own typo 'counter' for 'encounter'.

The only narrative boxed text in the template (area 'A. The Hidden Room') reads: 'A greasy, irate-looking dwarf in a stained leather apron with a bulging pocket stands between the contraptions. He clutches a handaxe in one hand and has a sock puppet on the other. “Go away!” the puppet snaps.' — exactly two descriptive sentences plus the one-line spoken tag, with concrete nouns (apron, pocket, handaxe, sock puppet).

verdicts.trueWording: Keywords should be CAPITALIZED and BOLDED the FIRST time they appear in the Background
verdicts.note: In the 'Background' section: 'Keywords should be CAPITALIZED and BOLDED the FIRST time they appear in the Background. This alerts the DM to the adventure’s more important aspects.' All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: doesn’t bloat the background with backstory that isn’t ultimately important
verdicts.note: 'There’s a fine line between two little [sic] background and too much exposition. Try to stay on the side of the line that doesn’t bloat the background with backstory that isn’t ultimately important.' Both limbs supported.
